cases.steps: Install and launch as a standard user. Open a ROM in a Unicode path with spaces. Save battery/state, close, reopen. Repeat from a read-only application folder.
cases.expected: Application starts without missing DLLs. Settings use the LocalAppData fallback when needed. ROM, battery save and state survive without corruption.

cases.steps: Check English and Russian menus/help. Resize from minimum to maximized. Move between monitors at 100%, 150% and 200% scaling. Restart with a secondary monitor disconnected.
cases.expected: Text and controls remain usable; menus map to the indicated actions; the restored window remains visible.

cases.steps: Use all eight buttons; remap two keys and cancel remapping. Hold A, Tab and Backspace while switching applications and opening a dialog. Return to the game.
cases.expected: No stuck input, turbo or rewind. Game auto-pauses/resumes when allowed. A manually paused game stays paused.

cases.steps: Enable the virtual console. Press each button, drag outside and release. Switch applications while holding a button. Use a scrollbar or drag in another Studio window.
cases.expected: Each button releases on mouse-up, capture transfer and focus loss. Other windows retain their own mouse capture.

cases.steps: Connect two physical pads. Test each button and stick in single-console and local Link modes. Assign device indexes, reconnect a pad and load/save profiles.
cases.expected: Players remain independent; mappings and deadzones persist; unplugging releases held buttons; reconnecting restores control.

cases.steps: Use a tilt-capable game and a rumble cartridge/game. Check numpad/right stick, pause, focus loss, controller reconnect and exit, including a mode that continues running in the background.
cases.expected: Tilt follows only focused input and returns to neutral. Rumble responds to cartridge events and stops on pause, focus loss and exit.

cases.steps: Run DMG and CGB games. Check all palettes, LCD/CRT, ghosting, raw comparison, Scale2x/3x, HQ2x and xBRZ at several window sizes. Save a raw BMP.
cases.expected: No clipped or corrupted frames. Effects change only presentation. Raw capture is 160x144 and matches the unprocessed framebuffer.

cases.steps: Repeat graphics checks with Direct3D enabled on the actual GPU. Toggle fullscreen repeatedly, minimize/restore, resize, move monitors and suspend/resume the computer.
cases.expected: Rendering recovers without stale frames or crashes. Device loss gives a usable CPU fallback. Record GPU/driver and hardware versus WARP.

cases.steps: Listen through actual speakers/headphones to pulse, wave and noise-heavy gameplay at all three rates and latency settings. Test volume/mute, channel mute and EQ.
cases.expected: Correct pitch/stereo, no persistent clicks, buzzing, clipping or desynchronization. Volume and mute controls take effect promptly.

cases.steps: While listening, pause/resume, rewind, use turbo, change speed, load a state and switch games. Unplug/reconnect the output device and change the Windows default endpoint.
cases.expected: No stale audio after transitions. Audio is muted at non-1x speeds. Device failure is visible and recovery behavior is recorded; no crash or hang.

cases.steps: Play for at least 60 minutes at 1x with actual audio output; include background/foreground changes. Record timing, underrun/overflow counters and a short end-of-run A/V recording.
cases.expected: No sustained speed drift, accumulating A/V offset, growing memory use, repeated underruns, freeze or crash.

cases.steps: Play, save battery data, use all quick slots, named states, rewind, reset and session restore. Try an incompatible state on a copy of the save.
cases.expected: Expected progress returns; incorrect states are rejected safely; original saves remain intact.

cases.steps: Connect a physical webcam, grant/deny OS permission, capture into a camera game, then disconnect and reconnect the camera. Test image-file input separately.
cases.expected: Actual camera frames arrive with usable orientation/contrast. Denial/disconnect is handled without a freeze. Record the device model and permission behavior.

cases.steps: Use supported printer/IR games. Print and export an image. Exchange an IR signal between the supported endpoints. State explicitly whether endpoints are emulated or physical.
cases.expected: Printer image and exported file match the game output. IR events reach the intended peer. Physical-device claims require actual hardware evidence.

cases.steps: Use two independent saves. Complete a local Link exchange and a network exchange on two computers. For Pokemon, complete a trade, save, close and reopen both games.
cases.expected: Both peers remain synchronized. Traded data and progress survive restart. Record both build hashes, game hashes and network conditions.

cases.steps: Record and replay input; export WAV/FLAC/AVI and inspect them in independent players. Exchange a BESS state with a named external emulator in both directions.
cases.expected: Replay matches the same ROM; media plays correctly and remains synchronized; both BESS directions preserve the expected state.

cases.steps: With a real test account, log in/out, unlock a test achievement, reconnect the network and verify Hardcore restrictions against the server response.
cases.expected: Credentials are not exposed in reports. Server confirms the expected account/unlock/Hardcore behavior; local UI alone is insufficient evidence.

cases.steps: On clean Windows 10 and 11 machines, extract/install the final package, run automated QA, verify every EXE/DLL signature, then uninstall while keeping saves.
cases.expected: No build tools are required. Automated checks pass for these exact binaries. Signatures validate if a signed release is claimed. Uninstall preserves user data.

scope: Human observations only. NOT_RUN and BLOCKED are open work, never PASS. Wine is not native Windows validation. Physical-device and audible claims require a human using the named actual devices.
